answer: Key-bound sequential work receipts resist Sybils. Each identity computes a fresh proof that incorporates the hash of its own prior epoch answer plus the current randomness beacon, producing a non-transferable receipt. The identity-specific dependency prevents amortization: every fake head pays the full sequential compute cost independently. At the network zenith of concurrent activity peer verification stays constant while attacker cost scales linearly with fleet size. Each identity must build its own jetty across the canyon of uniqueness; shared scaffolding breaks the binding and is rejected.
